title: Multiplayer Sprint B — server-authoritative bomb/blast/pickup/round-resolve (the headline cross-tab gameplay sync)
intent: S109 shipped Sprint A of GDP-2026-05-22-009 (connect-and-spectate): two tabs can connect, each sees the OTHER tab's bomber as a remote Presence entity with synced position + recipe. But each tab still runs its OWN bomb-fuse + blast-propagation + pickup + round-resolve locally — Tab A's bomb doesn't appear in Tab B's arena. The headline acceptance of GDP-2026-05-22-009 — 'Tab A places a bomb → Tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms; Tab A's bomb kills tab B's bomber; both tabs see the round resolve' — STILL pending. This is Sprint B: move bomb-fuse, blast-propagation, block-destruction, pickup-collect, pickup-spawn, round-resolve, bot-AI to the SERVER. Clients receive these as snapshot deltas + transient events. Local client systems for these become render/audio decorators that fire VFX/audio from the snapshot. The 'modern network game' from the user's 2026-05-20 ask FINALLY arrives.
rationale: GDP-2026-05-22-009 acceptance hints split this into Sprint A → D. Sprint A shipped (connect-and-spectate, recipe sync via Option B in S112). Sprint B is the user-visible payoff — without it, multiplayer is just a chatroom with avatars walking around, not a shared game. Sized as MUST because the rest of the multiplayer story (drop-in/out polish, snapshot relevance) is meaningless without cross-tab gameplay sync first. The architectural pieces are all in place: gameplay is grid-authoritative + deterministic + no Math.random/no wall-clock, exactly what the protocol contract expects. Sprint B is the integration sprint, not new design.
acceptanceHints: Builds on S109 connect-and-spectate (FEAT-MULTIPLAYER-FOUNDATION-T-001) + S112 recipe sync (FEAT-MP-RECIPE-SYNC-001).
Reference: existing docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md — extend with a Sprint B section before implementation. Spike sub-story may precede this if dev wants to derisk the server-side ECS port.
SERVER-SIDE (examples/backends/node-world-server, new kaboom-crew module):
Kaboom Crew rules ship as a server-side module. Port these CLIENT systems to server-side equivalents that act on the authoritative ECS world:
bomb-placement-system → validates PlaceBombRequest from client; spawns Bomb entity on server world
bomb-fuse-system → ticks fuseRemaining on every server tick; emits BlastEvent at zero
blast-propagation-system → walks the blast on the server; spawns BlastTile entities; flips alive=false on hit bombers (after Shield check); destroys soft blocks
pickup-spawn-system → server-side RNG (seeded by world seed + cell) decides pickup drops
pickup-collect-system → server detects bomber-cell-overlap; applies BomberStats updates
round-resolve-system → server detects ≤1 bomber alive; flips RoundState.phase; bumps tally; auto-restart after 3s
bot-AI-system → server owns bot decisions; empty player slots filled by bots
Server runs at fixed tick rate (e.g. 30 Hz). Snapshots emit at ~10 Hz (configurable).
Server seeds the arena from a per-world seed; pickup drops + bot decisions all use seeded RNGs — same world seed → same outcomes every time.
CLIENT-SIDE (examples/kaboom-crew):
In 'connected' profile, DISABLE the local bomb-fuse / blast-propagation / pickup / round-resolve / bot-AI systems. They become server-only.
Local systems that REMAIN client-side:
player-input-system → reads keyboard, sends inputIntent to server
grid-movement-system → client-prediction for LOCAL player only (remote players use interpolator)
death-animation-system → reads alive-flip from snapshot, fires ragdoll locally with blast direction from snapshot's BomberDied event
hit-recoil-system → reads shield-pop event from snapshot
voice-synth + audio-fx → fire from server-event deltas
HUD / minimap → reads from snapshot
PROTOCOL EXTENSIONS (schemas/protocol.schema.json):
placeBombRequest { entityId, gx, gz }: client → server
detonateRemoteRequest { entityId }: client → server (for Remote power-up)
inputIntent { entityId, dx, dz, tick }: client → server (movement input)
blastEvent { originGx, originGz, range, ownerId, cells: [{gx,gz}] }: server → client
pickupCollected { entityId, kind, gx, gz }: server → client
bomberDied { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz, killerId }: server → client
shieldConsumed { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz }: server → client
roundResolved { phase, winnerId?, tally, nextRoundAt }: server → client
blockDestroyed { gx, gz, droppedPickupKind?: string }: server → client
Each event opaque JSON; client decoder routes to local systems for VFX + audio.
CLIENT PREDICTION (movement only):
Local player's GridMover updates apply immediately on input (predict).

Server snapshot reconciles: if local grid position differs by ≤ 1 cell, smooth interp toward server value over 200 ms. If > 1 cell, snap. Remote players: interpolate via existing remote-bomber-interpolator-system.
No prediction on bomb placement — client sends placeBombRequest, waits for server's spawnBomb in snapshot. ~100-200 ms perceived latency on placement is acceptable for arcade pace.
DETERMINISM:

Server's RNG is the authority; clients trust snapshots. The existing bot-vs-bot regression test runs SERVER-SIDE and must continue to resolve within budget with bit-identical outcomes given the same world seed.
Client-side visual interpolation may differ tab-to-tab — acceptable per gameplay-systems.md §12.1 (visual determinism not binding).
PROFILE WIRING:
?profile=connected → networked path (default for two-tab playtest)
?profile=static → local single-player offline (unchanged from today)
?world=<id> → which server world to join (default 'test')
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST (the headline that's been pending since 2026-05-20):
Two Playwright tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected.
Tab A controls player.1 (or auto-assigned), Tab B controls a second bomber.
Tab A places a bomb → tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms.
Tab A's bomb chains into Tab B's cell → tab B's bomber gets the ragdoll launch + the killer's recipe seed propagates correctly.
Both tabs see the same RoundState (phase + tally + nextRoundAt).
Auto-restart fires identically on both tabs (within snapshot jitter).
BOTS IN MULTIPLAYER:
Server fills empty bomber slots with server-side bots. Each connected player gets a bomber, plus enough server-bots to fill to 4 total (configurable per world).
Bot personality / difficulty per world config (server-side, NOT per-client).
DIAGNOSTICS:
/__agf/network probe extends — peer count, last-snapshot bytes + latency, reconciliation jump count (already proposed in GDP-009).
Doctor section: 'Connected profile: server reachable, snapshot rate, reconciliation events last 30s'.
ROLLBACK PLAN:

If Sprint B reveals a perf or correctness issue blocking ship, the client retains the static profile path and the server skeleton stays available behind a feature flag. Connect-and-spectate (S109) keeps working as the multiplayer floor.
OUT OF SCOPE (Sprint C/D separately):
Drop-in/out behaviour for joins-at-mid-round (spectate-until-next-round) — Sprint C in GDP-2026-05-22-012.
5s reconnect grace on disconnect — Sprint C.
Snapshot relevance filter — Sprint D (deferrable; current 15×11 arena fits whole snapshot).
Lag compensation / hitscan rewind — no hitscan in this game.
Server reconnect-resume after server restart.
Custom rooms / lobbies / matchmaking.
Authentication / anti-cheat.
